input:
CURRENT SCENE:
一个人对神农说，麻烦我们可以吃什么植物？神农说，这就要看你想不想生病了。以后，神农告诉别人一些植物能吃，一些植物不能吃。

ITEMS:

[I355] 【麻烦】我们可以吃什么植物？神农说   correction: 麻烦 → 请问   strength: error
  checker's note: 麻烦 cannot directly introduce this question; 请问 is needed.
  rule card (search_find, Vocabulary): 找 means “look for.” Use 找到 when the person successfully finds something.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: the person successfully finds <object>, so use 找到, not 找.  Her terms: 找look for vs.找到find
  her past correction: 神农开始[-找]我们可以吃的植物
  her past correction: ⟦神农⟧开始找我们可以吃的植物 — her note: better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears
  her past correction: 神农开始找[-我们]可以吃的植物

[I356] 这就要【看】你想不想生病了   correction: 看 → 看到   strength: error
  checker's note: her pattern: 看 -> 看到 (corrected 37/71 in train)
  rule card (perception_look_see, Vocabulary): 看 is “look”; 看到 is “see/catch sight of” and shows that the person actually sees something. Use 看到 when the narrative gives the result of seeing.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: the person actually sees/catches sight of <thing or situation>, so use 看到, not 看.  Her terms: 看look vs.看到see, no了, 看look, 看到see
  her past correction: 他[看→看到]很多病人 — her note: 看look vs.看到see
  her past correction: 神农[看了→看到了]很多生病的人 — her note: 看look vs.看到see
  her past correction: 所以神农一[看→看到]病人就想找药 — her note: 看look vs.看到see

[I357] 一些【植物】不能吃   correction: 植物 → (delete)   strength: suggestion
  rule card (modifier_de_structure, Grammar): Use 的 after a modifier when it describes a noun, especially a longer phrase such as 人类创造的文明 or 能吃的植物. Do not add 的 after quantity words or fixed modifiers where it is not needed, such as 很多人, 一些人, 今天清晨, 蓝色衣服, and 好主意.  Pattern: <wrong> → <correct>: <modifier> describes the noun <noun>, so use 的; or <modifier> does not need 的 here, so omit it.  Her terms: no的
  her past correction: 可是一些[-的]人一吃植物 — her note: no的
  her past correction: 他们不知道什么植物[-能吃]不能吃
  her past correction: 吃很多[-的]植物

items.explanation: 麻烦 cannot directly introduce this question. Use 请问 to politely ask a question.
Use 看到 when the person actually sees or catches sight of a situation: 看 look vs. 看到 see.
It would be more natural to omit the repeated noun here: 一些不能吃. No 的 is needed.
